rong execution and growing demand for the Arm compute platform. Revenue reached $1.44 billion, up 27% year over year, marking our fifth consecutive quarter of year over year growth exceeding 20%. License and other revenue grew 50% to $773 million, while royalty revenue grew 8% to $670 million, with data center royalties doubling year over year. Non-GAAP earnings per share reached $0.52, up 33% year over year, while we continued to increase investment in R&D. AI is driving unprecedented demand for compute across the cloud, devices and autonomous systems, with Arm being the compute platform of choice. Our business is now driven by two area
ained data centers. Alongside our growing IP business, Arm AGI CPU expands our opportunity by delivering Arm-designed silicon directly to customers. Since launching in March, demand has continued to strengthen, with purchase orders secured from multiple customers extending through calendar 2027 and first commercial deliveries on track for fiscal Q4'27. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure plans to offer Arm AGI CPU instances in 2027, bringing Arm-designed and partner-designed processors together on a common platform and software ecosystem. 2 Our confidence in achieving up to $2 billion in Arm AGI CPU revenue over FY27–28 has increased over the last 90 days, supported by additional supply and customer mix. We remain focused on expanding capacity to meet growing customer demand. icer Investor Contact Investor.Relations@arm.com Media Contact Global-PRteam@arm.com 4 Q2 FYE27 Financial Overview • Arm's Q2 results demonstrated strong year-over-year revenue growth. Total revenue increased 27% year-over-year to $1,443 million, representing our best ever second-quarter revenue. • Royalty revenue increased 8% year-over-year to $670 million, driven by the c ontinued adoption of Arm technology with higher royalty rates per chip, such as Armv9 architecture and Arm CSS, and increased deployment of Arm-based chips in data centers. This was partially offset by the impact of memory pricing on the smartphone market. • License and other revenue increased 50% year-over-year to $773 million driven by continued strong demand for Arm IP, as well as fluctuation in the timing and size of multiple high-value license agreements and contributions from backlog. • Annualized contract value (ACV), a metric for normalized license and other revenue, increased 12% year-over-year to $1,790 million. • GAAP gross profit was $1,401 million, which equates to a GAAP gross margin of 97.1%. Non-GAAP gross profit was $1,412 million, which equates to a non-GAAP gross margin of 97.9%. • GAAP operating expenses were $1,200 million. Non-GAAP operating expenses were $774 million and increased 19% year-ov
in the same period a year ago. • N on-GAAP f ree cash flow (FCF) for the trailing twelve months was $1,096 million . • Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled $3,621 million .
